evidence.claim: The Bundestag reported that the Constitutional Court rejected the AfD's request to install its committee-chair nominees and explained that the committees had used a free majority vote to choose their chairs.
evidence.title: Gericht lehnt AfD-Eilantrag zur Ausschussvorsitzendenwahl ab
evidence.excerpt: The Bundestag reported that the Constitutional Court rejected the AfD's request to install its committee-chair nominees and explained that the committees had used a free majority vote to choose their chairs.
evidence.source_locator: opening summary and section 'AfD-Kandidaten nicht zu Ausschussvorsitzenden gewählt'
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official parliamentary report on a contemporaneous court decision affecting opposition office access.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 check on parliamentary competition and minority rights.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional rather than Scholz-personal; it reflects parliamentary autonomy under his government.
contrary_evidence: The majority could deny opposition nominees those posts.
That is a democratic contest mechanism, not evidence of entrenchment.

evidence.claim: The Federal Administrative Court held that a protest camp can generally be protected as an assembly under Article 8 of the Basic Law and that necessary infrastructure can also fall under assembly protection.
evidence.title: Versammlungsrechtlicher Schutz eines Protestcamps und seiner infrastrukturellen Einrichtungen
evidence.excerpt: The Federal Administrative Court held that a protest camp can generally be protected as an assembly under Article 8 of the Basic Law and that necessary infrastructure can also fall under assembly protection.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary domestic judicial ruling on assembly and protest protection.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 rule-of-law evidence on protest space.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional, not personal; the ruling reflects the legal environment during Scholz's chancellorship.
contrary_evidence: Authorities can still impose limits in some circumstances.
The decision concerns protest rights generally, not Scholz's personal behavior.

evidence.claim: The Court reiterated that press and broadcasting freedom protect the whole journalistic process, including access to needed information and sources, and that the state may not impose indirect pressures that amount to interference.
evidence.title: Beschluss vom 30. März 2022
evidence.excerpt: The Court reiterated that press and broadcasting freedom protect the whole journalistic process, including access to needed information and sources, and that the state may not impose indirect pressures that amount to interference.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Authoritative constitutional decision on media freedom and access to information.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 legal context for media freedom.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional, not personal; it establishes the constitutional framework under Scholz's government.
contrary_evidence: This does not show a specific Scholz initiative.
It is a general rights ruling rather than a case about media policy.

evidence.claim: The Court held that statutory rules requiring the transmission of personal data obtained by intelligence methods violated constitutional requirements of legal clarity and proportionality.
evidence.title: Erfolgreiche Verfassungsbeschwerde gegen die Übermittlung mit nachrichtendienstlichen Mitteln erhobener personenbezogener Daten
evidence.excerpt: The Court held that statutory rules requiring the transmission of personal data obtained by intelligence methods violated constitutional requirements of legal clarity and proportionality.
evidence.source_locator: press release body and opening paragraphs
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary constitutional review of surveillance-data transfer limits.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional, not personal; it shows judicial limits on surveillance under Scholz.
contrary_evidence: This is a legal limit, not an executive anti-surveillance initiative.
It does not demonstrate whether the government changed practice immediately.

evidence.claim: The Court ruled that the federal government's refusal to disclose the number of foreign-deployed constitutional-protection employees violated an MP's parliamentary question right.
evidence.title: Unterlassene Auskunft der Bundesregierung zur Zahl der im Ausland tätigen Verfassungsschutzbediensteten verletzt parlamentarisches Fragerecht
evidence.excerpt: The Court ruled that the federal government's refusal to disclose the number of foreign-deployed constitutional-protection employees violated an MP's parliamentary question right.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ruling on parliamentary oversight and executive disclosure duties.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional rather than personal; it reflects the strength of parliamentary oversight during Scholz's term.
contrary_evidence: The case concerns disclosure, not direct policy substance.
It shows a check on the executive, not an affirmative freedom-expansion program.

evidence.claim: The cabinet adopted a draft law to strengthen democratic participation, diversity, extremism prevention, and political education.
evidence.title: Bundeskabinett - Ergebnisse
evidence.excerpt: The cabinet adopted a draft law to strengthen democratic participation, diversity, extremism prevention, and political education.
evidence.source_locator: top section listing agenda items for the 44th cabinet meeting
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous official cabinet decision with clear policy content.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Cabinet-level action under Scholz; it reflects government policy rather than a personal order.
contrary_evidence: It is a draft-law step, not proof of downstream effects.
The proposal is preventive and indirect rather than a direct rights guarantee.

evidence.claim: Scholz used the Chanukka speech to reaffirm Germany's historical responsibility toward Jewish life and remembrance, linking the fight against antisemitism to the protection of Jewish life in Germany.
evidence.title: Rede von Bundeskanzler Olaf Scholz bei der Chanukka-Feierstunde in der Heinz-Galinski-Schule am 19. Dezember 2022 in Berlin
evidence.excerpt: Scholz used the Chanukka speech to reaffirm Germany's historical responsibility toward Jewish life and remembrance, linking the fight against antisemitism to the protection of Jewish life in Germany.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct Scholz speech in the federal bulletin archive.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 public stance on minority equality and protection.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Scholz rhetoric; this is public stance rather than operational policy.
contrary_evidence: Symbolic speech is not the same as enforcement or institutional reform.
It does not by itself show how anti-antisemitism policy was implemented.

unresolved_gaps: Direct evidence on internal nuclear-safety alternatives and command-and-control review is still thin.
Internal cabinet deliberations and precise alternative options around the Ukraine response are not visible.
Most policing and complaint-handling evidence is Länder-level, so direct Scholz attribution remains limited.
Direct evidence of 2022 Scholz-led democratic strengthening is thinner than evidence of institutional baseline and judicial constraint.
Direct chancellor-level evidence on personnel selection, correction after failure, and anti-capture choices remains limited.
Post-enactment delivery quality and longer-run durability of the reforms are not fully shown in the 2022 package.
Direct primary evidence on assets, gifts, family benefit, hidden conflicts, or formal self-dealing is missing.
The record remains allegation-heavy rather than adjudication-heavy on deception and obstruction.
Direct evidence on Scholz's personnel selection, correction of underperformers, and internal discipline is thinner than evidence on program design and rollout.
